subject: Re: Azure Marketplace co-sell readiness — licensing & SKU questions
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@cloudvista.com>
To: diego_fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 26 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Azure Marketplace: licensing & SKU mapping for integration

Hi Diego,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Our legal and procurement teams asked for two items to keep the marketplace onboarding moving: a clear mapping of our product SKUs to the Azure offer SKUs, and confirmation on licensing language (e.g., whether Redwood's terms map to per-seat or usage-based licensing in the listing).

Could you share a CSV mapping and a short statement we can include in our procurement packet? If there are expected changes to pricing or SKU splits for co-sell eligibility, flag those now so we can include them in our internal review.

We're on a tight timeline — aiming to submit the manifest by next Wednesday (6/2). Appreciate any attachments you can provide.

Alex Turner
Director, Strategic Partnerships
CloudVista Inc.

Attachment: CloudVista_Mutual_Action_Plan_v2.pdf (stub)
From: diego_fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@cloudvista.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 26 May 2026 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Azure Marketplace: licensing & SKU mapping for integration

Alex —

Thanks for the clear ask. Attached is a first-pass SKU mapping (SKU_Mapping_Redwood_vs_CloudVista.csv) and a short statement on licensing. Quick notes:

- Our listing supports usage-based pricing by default (tokens/sec for hosted API), but for co-sell deals we can surface a per-seat-like contracted SKU that maps to a monthly committed capacity SKU.
- For the manifest, map CloudVista "CV-Enterprise" to Redwood SKU "rf-enterprise-m-committed" (see line 3 in the CSV).
- Pricing deltas for committed SKUs versus on-demand are handled as part of the pricing attachment — if CloudVista needs a custom price, we will coordinate a reserved-capacity amendment (legal needed).

I copied Marissa for any marketplace manifest constraints and Naomi for procurement readiness (DocuSign/license language).

Next steps:
- Marissa: can you confirm the manifest JSON key names we should use for committedSKU and coSellIndicator?
- Naomi: Draft a 2–3 sentence licensing blurb that procurement can drop into the CloudVista packet.

Diego
Director, Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachments: SKU_Mapping_Redwood_vs_CloudVista.csv (stub), manifest-draft.json (stub)
From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: diego_fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>, Alex Turner <alex.turner@cloudvista.com>
Cc: naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 27 May 2026 11:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Azure Marketplace: licensing & SKU mapping for integration

Thanks — quick technical confirmation from the marketplace side:

- Manifest keys: use "skuId" for each SKU entry; include a boolean "isCoSellEligible" at the SKU-level. For committed capacity, add a custom property "committedSkuReference" pointing to the reserved SKU id.
- For CoSell indicator, Azure expects both the manifest flag and the publisher co-sell registration in Partner Center. We'll start the co-sell registration once CloudVista confirms the SKU names.

Alex — I ran the draft manifest against our lint tool and it produced two warnings (pricing.currency missing on one SKU, and description length for the free-trial SKU > 500 chars). I trimmed the description in manifest-draft.json; please replace the pricing.currency field with "USD" in the CV-entry.

Kimberly — can you confirm whether the co-sell indicator requires any extra evidence (I believe we need a joint demo recording as part of the co-sell dossier)?

Marissa Cole
Marketplace Technical PM
Redwood Inference

Quoted in reply: "On Tue, May 26, 2026 at 10:04 AM diego_fernandez@redwood.com wrote: > Attached is a first-pass SKU mapping..."
From: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@cloudvista.com>, diego_fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2026 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Azure Marketplace: licensing & SKU mapping for integration

Alex — quick follow-up from security/compliance and co-sell ops:

- Evidence: for co-sell registration Azure requests a short joint GTM plan (we can use the CloudVista_Mutual_Action_Plan_v2.pdf you shared) plus either a recorded joint demo or a 30-minute live walkthrough scheduled with a Microsoft co-sell rep.
- Procurement blurb (naomi_feldman please confirm): "Redwood Inference provides inference services under a usage- and commitment-based model. For Marketplace co-sell offers, committed SKUs represent reserved capacity billed monthly. Pricing and billing terms for committed SKUs are set in an addendum between Redwood and the customer and will be referenced in the Azure Marketplace listing."

Alex — if that language works, Naomi will prepare a DocuSign-ready clause and I will trigger the co-sell registration with Azure once CloudVista confirms the final SKU names.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head, Marketplace Ops & Compliance
Redwood Inference
